sentences.text: A new atlas linked changes in brain size and cell activity to shifts in daily habits and behavior observed in aging and Alzheimer's disease.
Specifically, parts of the brain that control metabolism, stress, and sleep cycles shrank and altered their gene activity as people aged or developed the condition.
Within these regions, immune cells in the brain became more inflammatory, while neurons that help regulate sleep and daily rhythms showed the biggest changes in their gene activity.
Computer models further identified signs of inflammation and genes that control the body's daily clock as strong indicators of Alzheimer's disease.
